meta.name: Kodak Kodachrome 200 Professional Film (PKL)
notes: Shared datasheet E-55 (KODACHROME 25, 64 and 200 Professional Films, Process K-14); the curves of this film are on printed page 5.

Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds (daylight, 1/100 second with a 0.20 N.D. filter), as printed; density falls with exposure (reversal film). The R curve is the highest, G the middle, B the lowest.

Spectral sensitivity: effective exposure 1.4 seconds, density E.N.D. 1.00 (equivalent neutral density); y is log sensitivity (reciprocal exposure in erg/cm2 required to produce the specified density) as printed. The low tails are drawn only part-way down on the sheet.

Spectral dye density: dyes normalized to form a visual neutral density of 1.0 for a 3200 K viewing illuminant; diffuse spectral density. The top curve (labelled Visual Neutral) is the sum of the three dyes and is traced as 'neutral'. No separate minimum-density curve is plotted.
Grain: 'Diffuse rms Granularity: 16' as printed, read at a gross diffuse visual density of 1.0 with a 48-micrometre aperture, 12X magnification.
Viewed by tungsten projection light (3200 K), the light the sheet normalises the dye curves for.
